tg.conclusion: Reviewed Telegram v0.137.0. New: `tg session list` replaces `tg account list` with no alias, `tg <profile> session status [--check]` says whether a profile is logged in and as whom, and the store moves to version 77. RU/ES changelog, commands, mcp, profiles, sessions and usage updated; image links point at v0.137.0. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.92.0 and none of its planned items shipped.

max.conclusion: Reviewed MAX v0.103.0 to v0.111.0 with the exact published command contract. New: `account remove --keep-data|--delete-data` (ends the MAX session, then erases the token, profile files and the shared layer's data for the profile; the bot token stays; refused while `max serve` runs), `store import` (synthetic data into a test store), `schedule pause|resume`, repeatable `--at`, `participants_count` and `muted:` in search and stats, part of a name in `from:`/`chat:` (`from:Name*`), part of a word in message text (`*word*`, three letters minimum, matched as written apart from case and ё/е), and `sync.progress` events in the run record. Changed: `contacts unlink` requires `--from person:<uid>|person:me`; `--offline` on a command that needs MAX answers `permission_error` (`offline.refused`, exit 5); `contacts context|prepare` read only accounts of the profile's sphere and return `accounts`; `list:` in message search is refused (`query.unsupported-field`); remote embeddings over plain `http://` are refused off this computer (`model.address-refused`); `search messages --timeout` can run up to 29 seconds; test-data people are hidden from people lists; a damaged store answers `configuration_error` (`store.damaged`) and blocks writes; the store moves to version 66 (cli-core 0.642.0, cli-base 0.96.0). Fixed: `messages sync --all` reports progress inside a chat, daily and one-time schedules wait out `rate_limited` up to six hours, `max serve` exits with code 3 when outdated so systemd starts the new version, and setting the clock back no longer blocks sync. Topic search now defaults to `embeddinggemma` (`--accept-terms` is a no-op). RU commands copy and EN/ES bot, changelog, cli-contract, commands, mcp, people, sessions, topic-search, troubleshooting and usage reviewed (pinned source links moved to v0.111.0). Native gaps left for max-cli: query-language.md does not describe the new search syntax (`*part*`, `from:Name*`, `muted:`, `list:` refused), the changelog does not name the topic-search model change, and empty-default option rows still print a pair of backticks. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.76.0; none of its planned items shipped.

zm.conclusion: Reviewed Zoom v0.72.0 to v0.82.0 from the changelog and the docs diff since v0.71.0. New: `remote-meetings` is gone and `meetings create|update|cancel|invitation` change a Zoom meeting or read its invitation (0.77.0; docs/remote-meetings.md became docs/meeting-management.md, with redirect stubs from the old URL); `meetings update <reference> --event-id` is now `meetings link`; `meetings list` also asks Zoom for meetings that ran and are not stored yet, and `meetings show` reads one again from Zoom (`meeting:read:past_meeting`); `--backend archive|server|both`; `search meetings` shows 20 hits by default; folders move under `zoom-cli`; one keyring entry per profile (`oauth:zoom:<profile>` under service `zoom-cli`) shared by every run, with a file fallback, and one token refresh at a time; a keyring that does not answer is named (`keyring.unreachable`); `zm session list` (0.81.0); cli-core 1.0 and cli-base 1.0 with store version 73, and MCP refuses local paths that name credential folders, a WireCat tool's folders or the message store (0.82.0). RU/ES changelog (0.72.0 to 0.82.0), commands, configuration, installation, mcp, search, security, sessions, usage, zoom-app and the new meeting-management page updated; the overview, the authored Meetings guide (now checked against v0.82.0) and compare follow the rename. Six site corrections that zm now carries itself were retired. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.71.0 and none of its planned items (recording calls you only attend, notes per meeting, speaker names, meetings someone else hosted, a reviewed preparation brief, backups on macOS and Windows, other platforms) shipped.

drive.conclusion: Reviewed drive 0.78.0 and 0.79.0 from the changelog and the docs diff since v0.77.0. May break callers: drive runs on cli-core 1.0 (0.78.0) and 1.2 (0.79.0), which move the message store to versions 74 and 77, and `session` is cli-core's shared sign-in command. `session list` answers a list with `profile`, `signed_in` and `state` and takes no query, so WireCat Desktop shows drive's profiles again. `session status` answers `state` and `scopes`, and `--check` asks Google whose the sign-in is. `session end` answers `ended`, `removed` and `why`, and `session start` takes `--answer-stdin`. Fixed: a read-only run reads a stored file's text with `files download` and no `--output`, which stays the owner's alone over MCP. Security: an MCP call cannot name a credential folder, a WireCat tool's folder or the message store. RU/ES changelog (kept in English, as before), commands, installation, recipes, security, troubleshooting and usage reviewed. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.77.0: `mirrors watch` as a background service and the Later items have not shipped.

memo.conclusion: Reviewed memo 0.150.0 to 0.154.0 from the changelog and the docs diff since v0.149.0. Added in these versions: `search all` reads a tracker's issues, projects and comments (Linear), with `tracker.list` to leave them out (0.150.0); deleting a person or an organization also deletes your notes about them and the people merged into that person (0.150.0); MCP no longer offers `schedule exec`, `templates preview --file`, `templates edit`, `templates reset` or `models consents set` (0.150.0); morning-digest fixes (0.151.0, 0.152.0); cli-core 1.0 and cli-base 1.0 with store version 73, and MCP refuses local paths that name credential folders, a WireCat tool's folders or the message store (0.153.0); `memo bots list|show|move` keeps bots apart from people, and `memo domain-lists update|list` (0.154.0). RU/ES configuration, mcp and people (new Bots section, what a delete removes) updated, commands and changelog follow the English reference, changelog sections kept in English, as before. Five site corrections (business, import, mail, people, usage) that memo now carries itself were retired, their RU/ES text moved into the translations. The roadmap is unchanged since v0.131.87 and none of its planned items (project evidence next steps, meetings in a person's context, faster search) shipped.

wa.conclusion: Reviewed WhatsApp v0.39.0 to v0.48.0 from the changelog and the docs diff. `wa account list` is now `wa session list` (no alias), and `wa session status` is new; `wa guide` and the scenarios page arrived in 0.40.0; `models chats` decides whether chat text may go to a model off this computer, `images read` hands one picture to a coding agent, `store migrate --no-backup` exists, and time options take dates, today, yesterday and 2h/7d. `session start` now waits until the phone says its history is complete, or 5 minutes with nothing new. Over MCP a write set to `ask` runs without a question, and `chats clear|delete` are not offered to an MCP app. RU/ES changelog (0.39.0 to 0.48.0, headings and intro now translated), commands, scenarios (new), archive, bot, mcp, profiles, sessions and usage updated; the other changed pages already matched through corrections. Corrections: 18 wa entries retired (upstream carries them; the mcp and roadmap ones would have printed their text twice), one added for the usage hedge "None of this has been checked on a phone yet." Roadmap: the Old files item is upstream now; "A guide command" is still under Next although `wa guide` shipped in 0.40.0, so a correction removes it until whatsapp-cli drops it. No other planned item shipped.

gcal.conclusion: Reviewed gcal 0.35.0 from its changelog and the docs diff since v0.34.0. May break callers: the MCP Registry entry no longer starts `mcp serve --profiles all`; `--profiles` is a required argument, so a client set up from the registry asks which profiles to serve. A client set up from the old entry keeps `--profiles all` until it is set up again. The overview (#189) is rewritten as a sales page: what you get, the ideas a newcomer would not guess (including that over MCP a delete does not ask), an example, why gcal against its comparison, a start and plain limits. RU/ES index retranslated and changelog updated and accepted. The roadmap did not change.

mail.conclusion: Reviewed mail-cli v0.32.0 to v0.37.0 from the changelog and the docs diff. 0.35.0 adds the `sync_since` setting and `inbox` (new mail sorted by the AI model the owner chose, with no agent) and makes the MCP Registry entry ask which profiles to serve; 0.36.0 adds the sender and run report to `inbox`; 0.37.0 adds `aliases`, moves to cli-core 1.0 and cli-base 1.0 (store version 73), answers `permission_error` for a refused place over MCP, stops offering `schedule exec` over MCP, and keeps mail in Sent yours whatever its From. RU/ES changelog (0.33.0 to 0.37.0), commands, configuration and usage updated; the three mail corrections still match and upstream does not carry their text. Site pages: the email guide names the profile `personal` (was `ya`), the comparison footnote no longer claims an `mcp serve --allow-writes` option, the overview says that over MCP a deletion set to ask runs without a question and points to `sync_since`. Roadmap unchanged: its one Next item, a live Gmail OAuth test, is still open in mail-cli; the review (MD-3) asks mail-cli to drop it as test provenance.

b24.conclusion: Reviewed b24 0.28.0 from its changelog and the docs diff since v0.27.0: `search all` by meaning of deal and lead activities after `sync --embed`, `synced[].saved` counting only changed rows, cli-core 1.0 with store version 74, `sync --rescan` and `--allow-deletions`, MCP no longer offering `schedule exec`, and `permission_error` for a refused folder; the roadmap is unchanged since v0.27.0 and neither Next item (contacts and companies from the local store, their custom fields kept locally) has shipped, and the RU/ES changelog and commands were updated and accepted.

pbx.conclusion: Reviewed asterisk-cli v0.8.0 to v0.11.0 from the changelog and the docs diff. 0.9.0 adds `account remove` (with `--keep-data`, `--delete-data`, `--dry-run`) and a "Remove a phone system" section on the install page, makes the MCP Registry entry ask which profiles to serve, and lets Desktop remove a pbx account. 0.10.0 moves to cli-core 1.0 and cli-base 1.0 (store version 73). 0.11.0 stops a read under `PBX_READ_ONLY` from creating a store. Upstream now carries the installation opening, the `asterisk` group, the remote-database and SSH-user steps and the ffmpeg line, so the three before-translation corrections for them are retired (their RU/ES text moved into the translations first); the changelog link correction now matches the v0.11.0 link. RU/ES changelog (0.9.0 to 0.11.0), commands, index and installation updated; the RU installation opening loses its long dash. Roadmap unchanged: the `meetings list` direction filter and the CEL log did not ship and stay under Later.

wordpress.conclusion: Reviewed wordpress-cli v0.3.0 to v0.4.0 from the changelog and the docs diff. 0.4.0 stops `sync --rescan` from lifting the deletion hold, adds the owner-only `sync --allow-deletions <count>` (not offered over MCP; usage now has a paragraph on a held sync) and moves to cli-core 1.0 and cli-base 1.0 (store version 73). Upstream now carries the WireCat Desktop section of the install page, the new install opening, the Profile step for non-administrators and the Desktop line in the overview, so the two before-translation corrections for them are retired (their RU/ES text moved into the translations first). RU/ES changelog, commands, index, installation and usage updated; the RU usage opening loses the «API говорит» calque. Roadmap unchanged: browser sign-in, plugin fields, WordPress.com sites and view counts did not ship and stay planned.

attio.conclusion: Reviewed attio v0.6.0 to v0.8.0 from its changelog, the docs diff between the tags and the generated command reference. New in 0.8.0: with the `activities` setting on, `sync` copies Attio meetings with the transcripts of their finished call recordings, put on the deals of the people and companies who took part (src/meetings.ts), needing `meeting:read` and `call_recording:read` (scope row in installation), no meetings without `meeting:read`, a call kept up to its first 20,000 characters (usage section "Notes and tasks on a deal", index Limits, roadmap). 0.7.0: built on cli-core 1.0.0 and cli-base 1.0.0, store version 73 that only cli-core 1.0 tools open, `store migrate --no-backup`, `sync --allow-deletions <count>` past the mass-deletion guard (owner only, not over MCP), a kind Attio could not list whole marks nothing deleted, `permission_error` for a refused folder over MCP, the commands contents list names `activities`. RU/ES of index, installation, usage, roadmap, commands and changelog follow the new source. Portal corrections added for index (opening and What you get gain calls), installation (update the other WireCat tools together) and usage (what to do when the guard holds a sync), to move upstream at the next bump. The roadmap is unchanged in Next and Later: one-click sign-in, custom objects and lists, webhooks have not shipped.

hubspot.conclusion: Reviewed hubspot v0.6.0 to v0.8.0 from the changelog and the docs diff. 0.7.0 adds `sync --embed` and search by meaning over activities, and changes `activities create --subject`: person:<n> and organization:<n> are now refs as `deals show` gives them, and a HubSpot id is `person:crm:<id>`; usage shows that form. 0.8.0 moves to cli-core 1.0 and cli-base 1.0 (store version 73, `store migrate --no-backup`), adds `sync --allow-deletions` (terminal only), holds the id pass when a kind could not be listed in full, and answers `permission_error` for a refused folder over MCP. RU/ES changelog, commands and usage updated; RU index and usage openings lose the «Знайте» calque, and RU usage fixes the two mistranslations of CR-19. Roadmap unchanged: its one planned item, browser sign-in as yourself, did not ship and stays planned. No hubspot corrections exist.
